'''Joy S. Gaylinn Reidenberg''' is an American [[Anatomy|comparative anatomist]] specializing in the vocal and breathing apparatus of mammals, particularly [[cetacea]]ns ([[whale]]s, including [[dolphin]]s and [[porpoise]]s).<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Joy S Reidenberg {{!}} Mount Sinai - New York |url=https://profiles.mountsinai.org/joy-s-reidenberg#research |access-date=2025-03-17 |website=Mount Sinai Health System |language=en}}</ref> She is best known as the Comparative Anatomist in the TV science documentary series ''[[Inside Nature's Giants]]'' where she has dissected a number of animals varying in species.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Patalay |first=Ajesh |title=Inside Nature's Giants: A gory attempt to disprove 'intelligent design' theories |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/culture/tvandradio/5613900/Inside-Natures-Giants-A-gory-attempt-to-disprove-intelligent-design-theories.html |access-date=2017-06-06 |work=Telegraph.co.uk |language=en}}</ref>

==Education==
Reidenberg became interested in animal science and art as a high school student.  She earned a bachelor's degree (B.A.) from [[Cornell University]] in 1983, a master's (M.Phil.) from the [[Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai|Mount Sinai School of Medicine]] Graduate Program in Biological Sciences in 1985, and a doctorate (Ph.D.) in Biomedical Sciences: Anatomy in 1988.  There, she worked with anthropologist [[Jeffrey Laitman]].{{cn|date=May 2026}}

==Career==
===Media===
In 2009, a British production company now known as [[Windfall Films]] approached her about coming to [[Ireland]] on short notice to help dissect a 19.8&nbsp;m (65&nbsp;ft) [[fin whale]] that had washed up on the south coast. She conducted the dissection, and the company was so happy with her performance that they asked her to become a regular contributor to ''Inside Nature's Giants'', dissecting a variety of animals (18 episodes in total), and explaining their anatomy..<ref>[https://www.nytimes.com/2012/02/07/science/joy-reidenberg-anatomist-builds-a-following-on-inside-natures-giants.html ''From Inside Lions and Leviathans, Anatomist Builds a Following'']. [[New York Times]], 6 February 2012</ref>  Reidenberg has also starred in the 4-episode series "Sex in the Wild" on PBS (known as "Born in the Wild" on [[Channel 4]] in the UK).<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.montereyherald.com/article/NF/20150831/NEWS/150839951|title='Big Blue Live' makes its US debut|access-date=2017-06-06|language=en}}</ref>  She was also featured in a 3-day live series called "Big Blue Live" on [[PBS]] about marine life in [[Monterey Bay]], [[California]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.dailynews.com/arts-and-entertainment/20150828/big-blue-live-on-pbs-explores-great-whale-migration|title='Big Blue Live' on PBS explores great whale migration|access-date=2017-06-06|language=en}}</ref>

===Academic===
Reidenberg is a professor at the [[Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai]]'s Center for Anatomy and Functional Morphology,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nycep.org/faculty/joy-reidenberg|title=NYCEP: Joy Reidenberg|publisher=}}</ref> where she teaches Human Anatomy (including gross anatomy, histology, embryology, and imaging).  She was also the Course Director for General Anatomy at the [[New York College of Podiatric Medicine]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nycpm.edu/preclinical.asp|title=New York College of Podiatric Medicine|website=www.nycpm.edu|access-date=2017-06-06}}</ref> from 2014 to 2020.

=== Spade-toothed whale dissection ===
On December 2, 2024, Joy Reidenberg participated in a week-long dissection of a 5-meter (16.4&nbsp;ft) male [[spade-toothed whale]] in [[New Zealand]]. She was one of three US anatomists to join the dissection which was the first of its kind, as only 6 specimens of the species have been recorded as of 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hutchins |first=Rob |date=2024-12-17 |title=Rare spade-toothed whale has nine stomachs and 'wisdom' teeth |url=https://oceanographicmagazine.com/news/rare-spade-toothed-whale-has-nine-stomachs-and-wisdom-teeth/ |access-date=2025-03-17 |website=Oceanographic |language=en-GB}}</ref>
